evidence: Clear hierarchical module structure with well-defined packages (mmseg/apis, mmseg/models, mmseg/datasets, mmseg/core, etc.)
High average maintainability index (mi_avg=92.4) and low fan-out (1.1) indicate cohesive, loosely coupled modules
Centralized builder pattern (mmseg/models/builder.py, mmseg/datasets/builder.py) with Registry pattern for extensibility
Shared core components (mmseg/core, mmseg/utils) used across modules, indicating tight internal cohesion
Configuration-driven design with extensive YAML configs in configs/ directory, typical of modern ML frameworks
Single deployable unit (setup.py, no inter-service communication patterns)
Layered separation of concerns: data pipelines, models, segmentors, losses, evaluation, APIs
Modular backbones, decode heads, and necks with clear interfaces (BaseDecodeHead inheritance hierarchy)
risks: Potential for tight coupling if builder patterns are bypassed
Risk of monolith scaling issues as feature count grows
Limited deployment flexibility compared to microservices
